payload.reason: The evidence indicates that both single-language and multilingual BERT models perform well in capturing syntax-sensitive agreement patterns, but does not definitively state that one outperforms the other across all contexts.

claims.text: Single-language BERT performs well on tasks involving structure-dependent agreement relations, achieving above 80% accuracy in experiments.
Multilingual BERT also captures syntax-sensitive agreement patterns but may perform worse in certain linguistic contexts compared to single-language BERT.
The performance of BERT models varies by language and task, making direct comparisons challenging.
